newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE Oct wheat limit down, new lows set in deferred.
newsitem.headline: WCE Oct wheat limit down, new lows set in deferred.

text.p: WCE feed wheat futures tumbled the $7.50 limit in spot October amid long liquidation while the rest of the board posted new contract lows, traders said.
October feed wheat ended at $179.00 a tonne.
Traders said a potential increase in deliverable supplies sparked commercial and commission house liquidation.
"Traders were looking for increased supplies of feed wheat,"he said. "Cool, damp conditions during the past few weeks in the western Prairies have increased feed wheat quantity."

Western barley ended lower in light trade. But commercial short covering and the lack of farmer selling left the market relatively buoyant compared to other feedgrains, which suffered bigger losses, the trader said.
November western barley was off $0.90 at $145.60.
Canola was under pressure from heavy fund selling and a weaker CBOT soy complex. "We also had commercial and local selling which was met by some scale down commercial buying," another trader said.
November canola lost $7.60 at $426.20 and October flax dropped $7.50 at $402.50 in sympathy with canola.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats)
